questions.stem: For binary random variables X and Y, the joint probabilities are P(0,0)=1/4, P(1,0)=1/8, P(0,1)=1/2 and P(1,1)=1/8, with arguments (X,Y). Find E[Y|X=1].

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: The joint density f(x,y)=c(x+y) for 0≤x≤1 and 0≤y≤1, and zero elsewhere. Find P(X+Y≤1), to four decimals.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: Find the minimum value of x²+2y² subject to 2x+y=8.

questions.subject: Networks
questions.stem: Two circuits have self-inductances L₁ and L₂, mutual inductance M and unity coupling coefficient. Both currents I₁ and I₂ are nonzero. Select all values of I₁/I₂ at which their stored magnetic energy is minimum.
questions.tag: Previously labeled 2025 EE Q52 (not independently reverified here)

questions.subject: Networks
questions.stem: Two clockwise mesh currents I₁ and I₂ share a 4 Ω resistor. The first mesh has an additional 6 Ω resistor and a 20 V source, while the second has an additional 8 Ω resistor and a 12 V source. Both sources drive their respective clockwise mesh currents. Find I₁ in amperes.

questions.subject: Networks
questions.stem: A reciprocal two-port has impedance matrix Z=[[5,2],[2,8]] Ω. The input admittance Y₁₁ with port 2 short-circuited is:

questions.subject: Networks
questions.stem: An initially uncharged capacitor C=100 µF is connected at t=0 to a 10 V source through R=2 kΩ. Find the capacitor voltage at t=0.2 s, to three decimals.

questions.subject: Networks
questions.stem: Which properties are necessary for a driving-point impedance of a passive RLC network?
options: It has no poles in the open right-half plane
Its real part is nonnegative for Re(s)>0
All its poles must lie strictly on the negative real axis

questions.subject: Networks
questions.stem: Three resistors 10 Ω, 20 Ω and 40 Ω are connected in star to an ideal balanced 3-phase 400 V line-to-line supply. The neutral is connected to the source neutral. Find the magnitude of current in the 20 Ω branch in amperes, to three decimals.

questions.subject: Networks
questions.stem: When determining the Thevenin resistance of a linear circuit containing an independent current source and a dependent voltage source, which operation is appropriate?
options: Open the independent current source and retain the dependent source
Short the independent current source and open the dependent source

questions.subject: Networks
questions.stem: A first-order low-pass circuit has transfer function H(s)=1000/(s+1000). Find its −3 dB frequency in hertz, to two decimals.

questions.subject: Networks
questions.stem: A series RLC circuit has R=10 Ω and L=0.1 H. Its angular-frequency bandwidth is:

questions.subject: Networks
questions.stem: A node V is connected to a 20 V node through 5 Ω and to ground through 10 Ω. A voltage-controlled current source of value 0.05V A draws current from the node toward ground. Find V in volts, to three decimals.

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.stem: During a power outage, a household UPS supplies a limited set of lights and fans. In a Newton–Raphson power-flow model of this isolated household system, the UPS is represented as:

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.stem: A three-bus network has prefault voltages of 1 pu. The relevant bus-impedance entries are Z₂₂=j0.25 pu and Z₁₂=j0.10 pu. A bolted three-phase fault occurs at bus 2. Find the magnitude of the voltage at bus 1 during the fault.

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.stem: A nominal-π transmission line has total series impedance Z and total shunt admittance Y. Its ABCD parameter A is:

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.stem: Three buses have lossless lines of reactance X₁₂=0.2 pu, X₁₃=0.4 pu and X₂₃=0.2 pu. Bus 1 is the slack with θ₁=0. Net active-power injections at buses 2 and 3 are +0.5 pu and −0.5 pu. Using Pij=(θi−θj)/Xij, find θ₂ in radians.

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.stem: For a balanced three-phase set of positive-sequence currents, select the true statements.
options: The positive-sequence component can be nonzero
All three phase currents are equal phasors

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.stem: A generator has sequence reactances X₁=0.2 pu, X₂=0.2 pu and X₀=0.1 pu, with negligible resistance. Its prefault phase voltage is 1 pu. For a solid single-line-to-ground fault with zero fault impedance, find the magnitude of faulted-phase current in pu.

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.stem: In an overcurrent protection system, primary and backup relays are coordinated mainly so that:
options: The backup operates before the primary
The closest appropriate primary relay trips first
The farthest relay always trips first

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.stem: Two generators have incremental fuel costs dC₁/dP₁=10+0.02P₁ and dC₂/dP₂=12+0.01P₂, with power in MW. Neglect losses and limits. For a total demand of 300 MW, find P₁ in MW, to two decimals.

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.stem: Select the correct statements about synchronous-generator transient stability.
options: Rotor-angle dynamics follow the swing equation
Increasing transfer reactance generally increases maximum transferable power
The equal-area criterion can analyze a single-machine infinite-bus system

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.stem: A transformer has leakage reactance 0.12 pu on a 50 MVA, 132 kV base. Find its per-unit reactance on a 100 MVA, 132 kV base.

questions.subject: DC Machines
questions.stem: For a separately excited DC motor with constant field flux, the electromagnetic torque is directly proportional to:

questions.subject: DC Machines
questions.stem: An unsaturated DC series motor operates at speed N₁ with current I₁. Its load torque is proportional to N². If speed decreases to 0.8N₁, find I₂/I₁, to four decimals.

questions.subject: DC Machines
questions.stem: In a DC generator, armature reaction primarily causes:
options: Distortion of the main field and a shift in magnetic neutral axis
A constant armature current regardless of load

questions.subject: DC Machines
questions.stem: A 4-pole wave-wound DC generator has 600 armature conductors, flux per pole 0.025 Wb and speed 1000 rpm. Find generated EMF in volts.

questions.subject: DC Machines
questions.stem: Select all correct statements about starting a DC shunt motor.
options: At standstill, back EMF is zero
A starter can limit initial armature current
The field circuit should be properly energized
Direct application of rated voltage always produces rated armature current

questions.subject: DC Machines
questions.stem: A 220 V shunt motor has armature resistance 0.5 Ω. At 20 A armature current, speed is 1000 rpm. Assuming constant field flux, find speed at 40 A armature current in rpm, to two decimals.

questions.subject: DC Machines
questions.stem: A DC motor operating in regenerative braking mode:
options: Returns electrical power to the supply
Always dissipates all energy in an external resistor
Must rotate in the reverse direction

questions.subject: DC Machines
questions.stem: A 20 kW DC generator has constant losses of 400 W and full-load copper losses of 900 W. Assuming copper loss varies as load fraction squared, find the fraction of rated load at maximum efficiency, to four decimals.

questions.subject: DC Machines
questions.stem: Select the true statements about commutation in a DC machine.
options: The current in a coil reverses as it passes through the brush zone
Commutation is unrelated to armature inductance

questions.subject: DC Machines
questions.stem: A separately excited DC motor has armature voltage 240 V, armature resistance 0.4 Ω, armature current 30 A and speed 1200 rpm. Neglect mechanical and iron losses. Find developed electromagnetic torque in N·m, to two decimals.
